en.html:
Flash. Flash. Flash.

So many flashes, no counting them. Here, gone. Here again, gone again.

As though a rain of light were falling over us.

...Or wait.
Was I getting it backward?

Was I the one racing through all those lights?

en.html:
At this point my understanding stood at seventy-five percent.

A very precise figure for a man who did not understand the remaining quarter. For all I knew, that quarter contained the part explaining why the first three quarters were wrong. Never mind. Seventy-five sounded respectable. Say 'I am confused' and nobody listens. Say 'twenty-five percent remains under consideration' and suddenly you are conducting research.

...I pushed ahead with what I had and simplified. Make the explanation fit inside the available head.

I tried to break that down. Not quite as bad as I had first thought, perhaps?

At least it seemed we would not find ourselves above Pangaea, or in some world where unknown intelligent beings had built an equally unknown civilization.

Kageaki"...And if something does, no such guarantee?"
Muramasa《Yes. Even temporarily, we'll be residents. Something could fix us in that time and place so that we can't get out.》

Suppose, for example, the place and time that caught us was the middle of a gunfight. Stand there doing nothing, and naturally a bullet would pass through us. Connection with that world: successfully established.

That was probably what Muramasa meant.

...Though at that point, our relationship with space-time might not be the first item requiring attention.
